reason: E1 shows that cold-rolled Cantor alloy has a lower OCP and that heat treatment (stress relief) changes potential and corrosion, supporting the premise about residual stress effects. E2 shows that at high sliding speed, frictional heat forms an oxide layer on a CoCrFeMnNi sample, but it cracks under load and does not reduce wear, directly contradicting the premise that the layer reduces wear and mitigates corrosion. The key premise that the layer is ultra-nanocrystalline and simultaneously reduces both wear and corrosion is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Friction-induced severe plastic deformation and local heating in CoCrFeMnNi promote in situ formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline oxide/hydroxide passivation layer.
This dynamically formed layer simultaneously reduces wear and mitigates corrosion.
Cold-rolled CoCrFeMnNi with residual stresses has a lower OCP and different passivation behavior than stress-relieved material.
At high sliding speeds, frictional heat can form an oxide layer on CoCrFeMnNi, but it may crack under load.
